name: CT-RATE
description: CT-RATE comprises 25,692 non-contrast 3D chest CT scans from 21,304 unique patients. Each scan is accompanied by its corresponding radiology report. The dataset includes 50,188 reconstructed 3D chest CT volumes (over 14.3 million 2D slices) paired with radiology text reports. Each volume is annotated with 18 abnormalities, supporting extensive validation and fine-tuning.

creator.name: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci et al.
creator.affiliation: University of Zurich, ETH Zurich, Istanbul Medipol University, Boston University, and collaborating institutions

citeAs: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci et al. Developing generalist foundation models from a multimodal dataset for 3D computed tomography. arXiv:2403.17834v4 [cs.CV] 30 Sep 2025
rai:dataCollection: CT-RATE consists of chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. The dataset includes non-contrast chest CT volumes acquired between May 2015 and January 2023, totaling 50,188 reconstructed CT volumes from 25,692 distinct CT experiments conducted on 21,304 unique patients. CT volumes are reconstructed with various techniques for specific diagnostic requirements. The patients range in age from 18 to 102 years, with a mean of 48.8 years and a mode of 40 years. The sex distribution is 41.6% female and 58.4% male. 61.5% of the scans are taken using Philips CT scanners, 30.1% with Siemens scanners, and 8.4% with PNMS (Philips-Neusoft Medical Systems) scanners.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Direct measurement
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Non-contrast chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. The radiology reports are structured into four sections: clinical information, technique, findings, and impression. The clinical information section outlines the patient's symptoms and medical history. The technique section specifies the acquisition protocol. The findings section covers anatomical and pathological observations, whereas the impression offers a diagnosis based on these findings.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each chest CT volume's orientation is standardized by examining its metadata to ensure consistency. All identifying information about patients and medical professionals is removed from the metadata. The radiology reports are anonymized by removing all personal information pertaining to patients and medical professionals using targeted searches with regular expressions to identify and eliminate date-related information and patient-doctor identifiers. The anonymized reports are translated from Turkish to English using the Google Translate API, and bilingual final-year medical students review and correct all translations.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each volume is resized to achieve uniform spacing of 0.75 mm in the x-axis and y-axis and 1.5 mm in the z-axis. The CT volumes are then either center-cropped or padded to reach a consistent resolution of 480×480×240. CT volumes are converted to Hounsfield Unit (HU) values using intercept and slope values from the metadata. HU values are clipped to a range of -1000 to 1000. During training, these values are normalized to a range of -1 to 1. Volumes that involve contrast material or body parts other than the chest are excluded.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: To develop an automated label extractor model, 1,000 reports are annotated by merging findings and impression sections, creating a multi-label dataset for each report, identifying 18 abnormalities. Conditions that are not referenced in either section are considered absent. Similar conditions are grouped. The annotated reports are divided into training (80%, 800 reports) and validation (20%, 200 reports) sets. A pretrained language model, RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m, is finetuned on this dataset and applied to classify the remaining 24,692 reports.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The finetuned model's precision, recall, and F1 scores show robust classification across abnormalities, ensuring the CT-RATE dataset is enriched with high-quality labels. These classified reports serve three purposes: training the supervised baseline model, finetuning CT-CLIP, and internal evaluation of the models.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each report is annotated with 18 distinct abnormalities for multi-label classification.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Bilingual final-year medical students reviewed and corrected all translations and examined each report to remove any residual personal information.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT-RoBERTa-4m (a pretrained language model finetuned for automated label extraction from radiology reports). TotalSegmentator was used to generate organ-level anatomical segmentation labels. A state-of-the-art 3D nodule segmentation algorithm was used to extract detailed nodule information.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Age (18-102 years), sex (41.6% female, 58.4% male), and geographic location (Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital, Turkey). All personal information pertaining to patients and medical professionals is removed from both CT volumes and radiology reports before open-sourcing.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The open-source release of CT-RATE, CT-CLIP, and CT-CHAT addresses critical challenges in 3D medical imaging and lays the groundwork for future innovations in medical AI and improved patient care. AI has the potential to address challenges by efficiently identifying pathologies, reducing the workload on radiologists, and potentially saving lives in situations where immediate radiological expertise is not available.
rai:dataBiases: Biases inherent to the single-institution dataset may influence self-supervised training. The data originates from a single geographic and clinical setting (Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital, Turkey), which may limit the generalizability of models to other populations. Variability in how diseases are described across radiology reports can affect detection accuracy. The dataset captures substantial heterogeneity in CT scanners, acquisition protocols, and reconstruction techniques, but is still limited to one institution.
rai:dataLimitations: CT-RATE is a single-center dataset from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital, Turkey, which may limit generalizability to other populations and clinical settings. The dataset does not represent a curated study dataset but rather reflects real-world scenarios characterized by heterogeneity. The current models are limited to chest CT volumes. The quality of generated reports remains insufficient for clinical use, underscoring the need for further improvements in performance and clinical validation. Substantial progress is still needed for clinical deployment in 3D medical imaging. Challenges such as robustness, interpretability, regulatory compliance, and prospective validation must be addressed before integration into routine radiology workflows.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is used to develop CT-CLIP, a CT-focused contrastive language-image pretraining framework designed for broad applications without the need for task-specific training, including multi-abnormality detection and case retrieval. CT-CLIP's vision encoder is combined with a pretrained large language model to create CT-CHAT, a vision-language foundational chat model for 3D chest CT volumes. The dataset supports tasks such as visual grounding, anatomical localization, and serves as a foundation for future fine-grained abnormality segmentation research.
